scope: Independent read-only wrapper/ring arithmetic challenge plus exact-rational high-ratio sample control. Original producer instructions inspected; full live-consumer byte/REA closure remains the separate native finding. No target code execution.
findings: CPRLiveStereoTransfer splits each converted block into <=8192 output-frame writes, immediately drains each into the appropriate planar buffer offsets, and preserves the same ring state across calls on one cursor.

This resolves the oversized-block concern: 8192 source frames at 8000→192000 can emit196585 output frames, exceeding the whole32768-frame ring. Converter block size and ring transfer size are separate.

Native producer checks free space before each frame against half-capacity; original100384b40..bac/bf8..c00 makes the whole-request bound free−16384+1 appropriate. The copied stereo path100384c44..c80 uses separate four-byte channel stores without mono gain.

C write preflight preserves state/storage on WOULD_BLOCK. Consume bounds end−start before narrowing and rejects signed overflow. Normal underrun, stopped and draining branches retain distinct read/timeline effects; the Swift adapter only invokes the sufficient-data branch.

The wrapper uses two independently allocated32768-float arrays and creates one transfer per cursor. Each output buffer is newly allocated and is not scheduled until all converter/gain/ring operations succeed.
No actionable defect found in the reviewed bounded adapter. This is a serialized value-operation integration, not the native thread/polling/callback graph or a full live scheduler.

independent_high_ratio_control.method: Pinned integer/Fraction helper rounds each native arithmetic operation independently. Candidate code is not used to generate sample bits. Compact retained digest/checkpoints avoid a large generated PCM artifact.
